summary: Kshanika Saha is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Calcutta (attested 1966) under the instruction of Nalinaksha Dutt.

Kshetresa Chandra Chattopadhyaya (1896–1974) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ganganatha Jha and at the universities of Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit. He served at Allahabad (from 1924) and directed the Research Institute at Sampurnanand (~1956–1968).

Kshitimohan Sen (1880–1960) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy after earning an M.A. at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He served in the Chamba State Education Department (~1904–1908) and held long-term posts at Visva-Bharati University, serving as Adhyaksha from 1953 to 1954.

Kumataro Kawada (1899–1981) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied and earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Japan Women's University (1927), the University of Tokyo (1950–1959), and Komazawa University (1959).

Kun Chang (1917–2017) was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua and Yale, where he earned his doctorate under Franklin Edgerton. He held posts at Academia Sinica (~1941–1947), the University of Washington (1951), and UC Berkeley (1963–1987).

Kunio Harikai (born 1942) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyushu University under Seiren Matsunami and Shoren Ihara, completing his BA and PhD degrees, and served as an associate professor at Saga Medical School (~1978–1993).
Kunio Iwaya (born 1943) studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1962 to ~1967 and held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from ~1972 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani (born 1948) is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He served as a professor at Kyoto University from ~1992 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka (1908–1993) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1931). He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

Kunio Yanagita (1875–1962) was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies who studied law at the University of Tokyo. He served in the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, the Permanent Mandates Commission, the Privy Council, and taught at Kokugakuin and Keio.

Kuno Fischer (1824–1907) was a philosopher who studied at Leipzig University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1856–1871) and Heidelberg University (~1872–1906).

Kuno Lorenz (born 1932) is a philosopher who completed his PhD at Kiel University and habilitation at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg. He held the chair of philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and was a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Kuno Meyer (1858–1919) was a linguist who studied under Ernst Windisch at Leipzig University (~1879–1883). He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1915).

Kuntala Bhattacharya specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA supervised by Prabal Kumar Sen and a PhD at Jadavpur University supervised by Amita Chatterjee and Shyamapada Misra, holding a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Kunzang Pelden was a scholar who studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. His students included Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.

Kurt A. Behrendt (born 1964) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1991–1997) and became an assistant curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (~2006).
Kurt Andrew Johnson is an Indology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of York in 2010 under the supervision of Jane Moody.

Kurt Huber (1893–1943) was a philosopher who earned his PhD and habilitation at the University of Munich (~1913–1920). He spent his academic career at the University of Munich, where he became an associate professor in 1926 and professor in 1938.

Kurt Tropper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Ernst Steinkellner, later holding posts as a Vertragsassistent at the University of Vienna and at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
